Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:10:1.hebrew: במאי עסקינן - דאצטריך ליה למיתני ח"נ, ולא תנא רבי יעקב מחייב:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:10:1.english: With what are we dealing - That it was necessary for [the Tanna] to teach "half-damage," and he did not teach [simply] "Rabbi Ya'akov obligates [him]."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:10:2.hebrew: אי דעבד ליה שמירה - מעולה, ונפרצה בלילה או שפרצוה לסטין, משום הכי פטר ליה מנזק שלם — כלל כלל לא בעי לשלומי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:10:2.english: If he provided safeguarding for it - [i.e.,] superior [safeguarding], and it was breached at night or bandits breached it — for that reason [the law] exempts him from full damage; he does not need to pay at all.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:10:3.hebrew: ואי דלא עבד ליה שמירה - מעולה, כוליה נזק בעי לשלומי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:10:3.english: And if he did not provide it with safeguarding - superior [safeguarding], he must pay the entire damage.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:11:1.hebrew: שמירה פחותה - נעל בפניה כראוי, ואמרינן [לקמן] (ד' נה:): דלת שיכולה לעמוד ברוח מצויה — זהו כראוי, והיינו שמירה פחותה אצל רוח שאינה מצויה. ואצטריך לאשמועינן דמשתלם ח"נ ולא כולו, ולאפוקי מהני תנאי דפליגי בשילהי פירקין, דאיכא למ"ד דפטור, ואיכא דמחייב ליה נזק שלם. ואשמועינן הכא דרבי יעקב סבר לה כרבי יהודה, דאמר בשילהי פירקין: במועד סגי ליה בשמירה פחותה, דמייתרי ביה קראי, ומפטר מנזק שלם; ומיהו בחצי נזק מחייב, כדאמרינן לקמן: לא פטר ר' יהודה אלא על צד העדאה שבו, אבל צד תמות במקומה עומדת, ותם לא סגי ליה בשמירה פחותה דלא מייתרי ביה קראי. ואע"ג דהך צד תמות מגופיה משתלם, אית ליה לר' יעקב מעמידין אפוטרופוס לתם לגבות מגופיה, כרבנן דפליגי עליה דסומכוס לעיל:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:11:1.english: Reduced safeguarding - [He] locked [the door] before it properly, and we say later (55b): a door that can withstand an ordinary wind — this is [considered] "properly," and this is reduced safeguarding with respect to an extraordinary wind. And it was necessary to teach us that he pays half-damages and not all of it, to exclude those Tannaim who dispute at the end of our chapter, where there is one who says he is exempt and there is one who holds him liable for full damages. And it teaches us here that Rabbi Ya'akov holds like Rabbi Yehudah, who says at the end of our chapter: for a forewarned [ox], reduced safeguarding suffices for it, since the verses are superfluous with respect to it, so it is exempt from full damages; however, for half-damages he is liable, as we say later: Rabbi Yehudah only exempted [it] with respect to its aspect of being forewarned, whereas the aspect of being innocuous remains in place, and for an innocuous [ox], reduced safeguarding does not suffice, since the verses are not superfluous with respect to it. And even though this innocuous aspect is paid from its [own] body, Rabbi Ya'akov holds [that] we appoint a guardian for an innocuous [ox] to collect from its body, like the Rabbis who dispute Symmachus above.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:14:1.hebrew: ולא פליגי - ר' יעקב ורבי יהודה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:14:1.english: And do they not disagree - Rabbi Yaakov and Rabbi Yehuda.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:15:1.hebrew: ולאביי דאמר פליגי במאי פליגי - אי בתם, לא קאמר רבי יהודה נ"ש. ואי במועד ושמירה פחותה, הא שמעינן ליה לרבי יהודה אפילו בשור של פיקח ח"נ ותו לא. ואי בדלא נטריה כלל, מאי טעם דר' יעקב:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:15:1.english: And according to Abaye, who says they disagree, with regard to what do they disagree - If [they disagree] regarding a tam [innocuous ox], Rabbi Yehuda would not say [that he pays] full damages. And if [they disagree] regarding a mu'ad [forewarned ox] with inferior guarding, we have already heard Rabbi Yehuda [say] even regarding the ox of a mentally competent person [that he pays] half damages and nothing more. And if [they disagree] where he did not guard it at all, what is the reason of Rabbi Ya'akov?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:16:1.hebrew: ולא נטריה כלל - וקאמר רבי יהודה נ"ש, החצי מן העלייה והחצי מן גופו, דשמעינן לרבי יהודה לקמן דכל תם ונעשה מועד, צד תמות במקומה עומדת ומגופו נגבית. והאי, אע"ג דלית ליה בעלים בני דעה, מעמידין אפוטרופוס לתם לגבות מגופו צד תמות:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:16:1.english: And he did not safeguard it at all - And Rabbi Yehudah says [that he pays] full damage: half from the superior [property] and half from its body; for we learn [regarding] Rabbi Yehudah later [on] that [for] any innocuous [ox] that became forewarned, the innocuous aspect remains in its place and is collected from its body. And [regarding] this one, even though it does not have owners of sound mind, they appoint a guardian for the innocuous [aspect] to collect the innocuous aspect from its body.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:17:1.hebrew: ורבי יעקב סבר לה כרבי יהודה בחדא - דכל תם ונעשה מועד, צד תמות במקומה עומדת לגבות מגופו. הלכך, הכא פטור מצד תמות, דבהך פליג עליה, דקסבר אין מעמידין אפוטרופוס לתם כו':
Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:17:1.english: And Rabbi Ya'akov holds in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda with regard to one [issue] - For [with] any innocuous [ox] that became forewarned, the element of innocuousness remains in its place, to collect from its body. Therefore, here [the owner] is exempt from the element of innocuousness, for in this [matter] he disagrees with him, as he holds [that the court] does not appoint a steward for an innocuous [ox], etc.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:18:1.hebrew: בשלמא לאביי דאמר פליגי שפיר - מוקי לה במועד למתניתא קמייתא, דבתם ליכא לאוקמא לאשמועינן דמעמידין אפוטרופוס לתם, דאשמועינן ליה במתניתא בתרייתא דאמר אין מעמידין. הלכך, ע"כ קמייתא נמי במועד, ולא נטריה כלל, ומשלם ח"נ דמועדת:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:18:1.english: Granted, according to Abaye, who says [that] they disagree, [it works out] well - [he] interprets the first baraita as referring to a forewarned [ox], for it is impossible to interpret it [as referring] to an innocuous [ox] to teach us that we appoint a guardian for an innocuous [ox], since we [already] heard it in the latter baraita, where he says we do not appoint [one]. Therefore, necessarily, the first [baraita] also [refers] to a forewarned [ox], where he did not guard it at all, and he pays the half-damages of a forewarned [ox].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:18:2.hebrew: אלא לרבא דאמר לא פליגי - ואית ליה לר' יעקב, מעמידין אפוטרופוס לתם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:18:2.english: But according to Rava, who says they do not disagree - and Rabbi Yaakov holds [that] we appoint a guardian for an innocuous [ox].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:18:3.hebrew: אדמוקי לה - לקמייתא במועד, לוקמא בתם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:18:3.english: Instead of interpreting it - [That is,] the first [baraita as referring] to a forewarned [ox], let him interpret it [as referring] to an innocuous [ox].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:1:1.english: They will refrain and not act - [as] a steward.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:1:2.english: From the superior-quality [property] of the steward - Because he did not guard it properly.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:1:3.hebrew: וחוזרין ונפרעין מן היתומים לכי גדלי - דאי לא, ממנעי ולא עבדי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:1:3.english: And they subsequently collect from the orphans when they grow up - For if not, [people] would refrain and not act [as stewards].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:4:1.english: [It] has reverted to its [status of] innocuousness - Later [the Gemara] explains what he is saying.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:5:1.english: What [is meant by] "it retains its innocuousness" that Sumakhos said - In the first clause.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:5:2.hebrew: אילימא דלא מייעד - בשלש נגיחות, לשלם מעלייה כשהועד:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:5:2.english: If we say that it is not rendered forewarned - through three gorings, to pay from [the owner's] superior [property] when it is forewarned.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:5:3.hebrew: הא מדקתני סיפא נתפקח החרש חזר לתמותו - דקסבר רשות משנה, מכלל דמעיקרא אייעד ליה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:5:3.english: From [the fact] that the latter clause teaches, "[If] the deaf-mute regained his faculties, it reverts to its [status of] innocuousness" - For he holds [that a change of] domain changes [its status], [it follows] by inference that initially it had been rendered forewarned.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:6:1.hebrew: הרי הוא בתמימותו - דלא גבי נגיחות תמות מיניה, דאין מעמידין אפוטרופוס לתם לגבות מגופו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:6:1.english: It retains its completeness - That [the injured party] does not collect [for] the gorings of [its] innocuousness from it, because [the court] does not appoint a steward for an innocuous [ox] to collect from its body.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:7:1.hebrew: רשות משנה - הרשות שנשתנה לה, שיצא מידי אפוטרופוס ונכנס לרשות בעלים, משנה את העדאתו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:7:1.english: Custody changes [it] - The custody to which [the ox] was changed — in that it left the hands of the guardian and entered the custody of the owner — changes its forewarning status.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:8:1.hebrew: ה"ג - ר' יעקב משלם ח"נ:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 39b:8:1.english: This is how we read [the text] - Rabbi Yaakov pays half-damages.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 39b:10:1.hebrew: אי בתם פשיטא - וכ"ת דאשמועי' דמעמידין אפוטרופוס לתם, א"כ ה"ל למתני: "ר' יעקב מחייב" ותו לא; ומדנקט ח"נ, משמע דאיצטריך דלא נימא נזק שלם:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 39b:10:1.english: If [it is] with regard to an innocuous [ox], [isn't this] obvious? - And if you should say that [Rabbi Ya'akov] is teaching us that we appoint a guardian [even] for an innocuous [ox], if so, [it] should have taught "Rabbi Ya'akov obligates [payment]" and nothing more; and since he stated "half-damage," it implies that it was necessary [to specify half-damage] so that we would not say [he pays] full damage:

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 39b:17:1.hebrew: ולא משלם אלא פלגא דמועד - ורבא לא בעי לשנויי הכי, מדלא קתני: "ר' יהודה אומר חייב נ"ש, ור' יעקב אומר ח"נ". ועוד, דמשמע ליה לרבא, דכיון דלא נטריה כלל, ה"ל למתני "אין משלם אלא חצי נזק", שזהו החידוש; ומדקאמר "משלם ח"נ", משמע דקמ"ל דמשלם אפילו ח"נ. אבל השתא דנטריה שמירה פחותה, חידוש הוא דקמ"ל דמשלם אפילו ח"נ. ועוד, דמשמע ליה ח"נ מגופו, כסתם ח"נ דבכל מקום:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 39b:17:1.english: And he pays only the half [due to its] forewarned [status] - And Rava did not want to answer this way, since [the baraita] does not teach: "Rabbi Yehuda says he is liable for full damages, and Rabbi Yaakov says half damages." And furthermore, it seems to Rava that since he did not guard it at all, [the Tanna] should have taught "he pays only half damages," for that is the novelty; and since [the Tanna] says "he pays half damages," it implies that he is teaching us that he pays even half damages. However, now that he guarded it with an inferior guarding, it is a novelty that he teaches us that he pays even half damages. And furthermore, "half damages" implies to him [that it is collected] from its body, like standard "half damages" everywhere.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 39b:18:1.hebrew: אדמוקי לה במועד לוקמיה בתם - תימה: דמעיקרא הוה פריך "אי בתם — פשיטא", ולא הוה בעי למימר דאתא לאשמועינן דמעמידין אפוטרופוס לתם, כדפי' לעיל, דאם כן ה"ל למימר "רבי יעקב מחייב"; והשתא פריך לאוקמיה בתם! וי"ל: דהשתא דאסיק אדעתיה דאמר "צד תמות במקומה עומדת", לא מצי למתני "רבי יעקב מחייב", דאיצטריך להזכיר ח"נ לאשמועינן דמעמידין אפוטרופוס לתם; ואי הוה תני "מחייב", הוה מוקמינן לה במועד — אבל תם פטור, דאין מעמידין אפוטרופוס לתם — ואיצטריך לאשמועינן דמועד משלם נ"ש, לאפוקי ממ"ד "צד תמות במקומה עומדת". אבל מעיקרא, דלא הוה אסיק אדעתיה "צד תמות כו'", פריך שפיר "אי בתם — פשיטא"; דאי לאשמועינן "מעמידין אפוטרופוס לתם" אתא, לתני "מחייב", והוה מוקמינן ליה בתם, דלמועד לא איצטריך:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 39b:18:1.english: Instead of interpreting it as referring to a forewarned [ox], let him interpret it as referring to an innocuous [ox] - This is puzzling: for initially [the Gemara] asked, "If [it refers] to an innocuous [ox], it is obvious!" — and did not want to say that [the baraita] comes to teach us that we appoint a guardian for an innocuous [ox], as I explained above, because if so, it should have stated, "Rabbi Yaakov holds [him] liable" — yet now it asks to interpret it as referring to an innocuous [ox]! And one can say: Now that it has entered [the Gemara's] mind [to consider the view] that says "the innocuous component remains in its place," [the baraita] could not have taught "Rabbi Yaakov holds [him] liable," because it was necessary to mention "half-damages" in order to teach us that we appoint a guardian for an innocuous [ox]. For if it had taught "holds [him] liable," we would have interpreted it as referring to a forewarned [ox] — whereas an innocuous [ox] is exempt, because we do not appoint a guardian for an innocuous [ox] — and [understood that] it was necessary to teach us that a forewarned [ox] pays full damages, to exclude [the view of] the one who says "the innocuous component remains in its place." However, initially, when it had not yet entered [the Gemara's] mind [to consider] "the innocuous component [remains in its place]," etc., it rightly asked, "If [it refers] to an innocuous [ox], it is obvious!" — for if it came to teach us [that] "we appoint a guardian for an innocuous [ox]," let it teach "holds [him] liable," and we would have interpreted it as referring to an innocuous [ox], since for a forewarned [ox] it would not be necessary.
